'''Avraham (Avi) Gover''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: אברהם גובר; born: 6 July 1945) is an Israeli professor of [[Electrical Engineering]] in the Physical Electronics Department of the [[Engineering]] Faculty at [[Tel Aviv University]], specializing in [[Quantum Electronics]] and FEL ([[free-electron laser]]) [[Physics]]. Gover is also the head of the Israeli Center for Radiation Sources and Applications (FEL Knowledge Center) in [[Ariel University|Ariel]].  In 2005, he was awarded the international FEL prize "in recognition for his outstanding contributions to Free Electron Laser science and technology".<ref name=fel_prize>{{citation|title=2005 International Free Electron Laser Prize Winner: Avi Gover |url=https://www-ssrl.slac.stanford.edu/lcls/fel2005/|publisher=[[Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource]]}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Avraham Gover was born in [[Lviv]], [[Soviet Union]] to [[holocaust]] survivor parents – Hella and Aharon Graubart, and emigrated to [[Israel]] with his family in 1949. He studied at "Kugel" high school in [[Holon]], and served in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] as a communications officer.  
He received his [[B.S.]] in Physics with distinction in 1968, and his [[M.S.]] in [[Solid State Physics]] with special distinction (1971) from Tel Aviv University.
 
His [[Ph.D.]] degree was received in 1975 from [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech). Under the supervision of Prof. [[Amnon Yariv]], Gover authored the thesis Wave Interactions in Periodic Structures and Periodic Dielectric Waveguides, laying foundation for the theory of electron beam radiators and Free Electron Lasers (FEL) in the high gain regime.<ref>{{citation|title=Wave Interactions in Periodic Structures and Periodic Dielectric Waveguides |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/33749947.pdf|publisher=Caltech|bibcode=1976PhDT........49G|last1=Gover|first1=A.|year=1976}}</ref><ref name=fel_prize/>
 
During his M.S. studies, Gover was a consultant at [[Tadiran]] Transistors Plant, involved in the first development of Integrated Circuits in Israel. During his Ph.D. studies, Gover was also a consultant at Meret - Electro-Optic Industry and at Heliotech, division of [[Spectrolab]], involved in first development of Vertical Multi-Junction [[Solar Cells]].<ref name=cv>{{citation|title=Prof. Avraham Gover|url=http://www.eng.tau.ac.il/~gover/biograph.html|publisher=Tel Aviv University|access-date=6 January 2020|archive-date=19 August 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070819054851/http://www.eng.tau.ac.il/~gover/biograph.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
 
 
==Academic career==
In 1976 Gover became a [[Research Fellow]] in Caltech, and in 1977 he joined Tel Aviv University as a [[Senior Lecturer]] in the Department of Physical Electronics of the Engineering faculty of Tel Aviv University. 
Gover served as the Head of the Kranzberg Institute of Electronic Devices Research, at Tel Aviv University in 1984-1985, and became a [[full professor]] in 1991.<ref name=cv/>
 
In 1988, Gover founded and headed a consortium for the development of the first Israeli FEL facility, including Tel-Aviv University, [[Weizmann Institute]], [[RAFAEL|Rafael Advanced Defense Systems]] and [[Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center|NRC]]. The consortium was steered by [[Yuval Neeman]], the Israeli [[Ministry of Science, Technology and Space|Minister of Science and Technology]] at the time. First lasing was demonstrated on Weizmann’s Electrostatic Tandem Accelerator in 1998.
 
In 2003 Gover founded the FEL National Knowledge Center for Radiation Sources and Applications of the Israeli Ministry of Science – a collaboration of Tel Aviv and [[Ariel University|Ariel Universities]] – and he heads it since.<ref>{{citation|title=Team – The Schlesinger Center |url=https://www.ariel.ac.il/wp/fel/people/ |publisher=Ariel University}}</ref>
Gover was holding the Ludwig Jokel Chair of Electronics at Tel-Aviv University during 2006-2010, and in 2011 he retired from Tel Aviv as professor emeritus.
Gover has mentored over 40 Master and PhD students and postdocs in the Faculty of Engineering, Physical Electronics Department and the Physics Department at Tel Aviv University. He also co-advised 3 PhD students in [[UCLA]] Physics Department, CA, USA.
 
During his sabbaticals, Gover was a visiting professor at [[Stanford University]], [[Brookhaven National Lab]], N.Y, [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], [[University of Maryland, College Park]], and [[University of California, Los Angeles|University of California, L.A.]] He was also a Cheng Tsang Man [[Financial endowment|Endowed Professor]] at the [[Nanyang Technological University]], [[Singapore]].<ref name=cv/>

==Research==

Gover’s research areas include: [[Quantum electronics]], [[electromagnetics]], [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]], [[electro-optics]], [[laser]]s, [[electronic devices]], [[semiconductors]] and [[semiconductor devices]].
His specific research topics are:				 
* free-electron [[quantum optics]]. 
* Interaction of quantum electron [[wavefunction]] with [[light]] and [[matter]].
* Electron beam interaction with [[electromagnetic radiation|electromagnetic waves]], free electron lasers, [[Cherenkov radiation|Cerenkov-Smith-Purcell radiation]].
* [[Superradiance]] and Stimulated Superradiance of bunched electron beams and [[shot-noise]] [[Electromagnetic interference|suppression]].
* [[Extremely high frequency|Millimeter Waves]] and [[Terahertz radiation|THz radiation]].
* Radiative [[energy transmission]] in [[free space]].<ref name=cv/>
 
Gover’s main research activity concentrates presently on fundamental theoretical investigation of the quantum electron wavefunction interactions with light and matter and the transition of free electrons from quantum to classical expression ([[wave particle duality|wave-particle duality]]). On this subject, and on subjects of laser [[particle acceleration|particle accelerator]], ultra-fast electron [[microscopy]] and compact free electron radiation sources from THz to [[X-ray]], he collaborates with front-line research laboratories in the [[US]] and [[Germany]].
 
In 2005 Gover was awarded the International FEL Prize “For outstanding contribution to Free Electron Laser science and technology”. In 2007 he became an [[IEEE]] fellow "For contributions to free electron lasers and superradiant bunched e-beam radiators".<ref>{{citation|title=IEEE Fellow|url=http://www.eng.tau.ac.il/research/FEL/images/ELA/IEEE%20Fellow.jpg|publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref> 
In 2008 he became a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "For outstanding scientific achievements and leadership in international cooperation in the area of Free Electron Lasers".<ref>{{citation|title=American Physical Society - Certificate of Fellowship |url=http://www.eng.tau.ac.il/research/FEL/images/ELA/APS%20Fellow.jpg |publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref> 
 
==Professional Experience==
Gover was consultant at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|Naval Research Lab.]] Plasma Div., [[Washington, D.C.]], U.S. in 1978-1984. He was the Principal Investigator on the [[Strategic Defense Initiative]] Office (SDIO) contract on Free Electron Lasers in Science Applications International Corporation, Plasma Physics Division in 1987-1988, and the head of the Israeli FEL consortium (TAU, RAFAEL, NRC) in the years 1992-2000.<ref name=cv/>
During 1988-1993 Gover served the FEL community in the Executive [[Committee]] of the International FEL Conference and in its FEL prize sub-committee.
In 2005 he served as a member of the "Soft X-ray Free Electron Laser Committee" of [[data infrastructure|ESFRI]] (EU), in charge of preparing a road map of the long term scientific infrastructure development of the [[European Commission|European Union Commission]].<ref name=cv/>
 
Gover was one of the founders of the Israeli National Inter-Senate Committee for Academic Independence, and served in it as the representative of Tel-Aviv University 2004-2013.<ref>{{citation|title=THE ISRAELI INTER-SENATE COMMITTEE (ISC) OF THE UNIVERSITIES FOR THE PROTECTION OF ACADEMIC INDEPENDENCE  |url=http://math.haifa.ac.il/YAIR/sub34_1.pdf |publisher=[[Haifa University]]}}</ref> 
 
 
==Publications==
Prof. Gover has authored over 250 scientific publications, and six patents.<ref>{{citation|title=inventor:(Avraham Gover) |url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Avraham+Gover |publisher=[[Google Patents]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gover is married to Joan. They have three children.
